title: Information Discernment in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2607.19355v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used with external knowledge sources like the internet. Do they weigh information appropriately -- updating more for reliable sources (source discernment) and more when claims bring priors closer to the truth (truth discernment)? We formalize this as information discernment and introduce Learn2Discern (L2D), an experimental framework and benchmark grounded in three normative axioms with interpretable metrics. To establish external validity, a pre-registered, quota-matched user study (n=299) confirms that real LLM users endorse all three axioms and report that violations reduce their trust and usage intent. Across 13 models and nearly 670K trials, we find consistent failures across both dimensions: models perform near chance on source and truth discernment, rely on source popularity twice as much as source reliability, and update roughly equally whether a claim improves or worsens their position relative to the g

translated_title: 大语言模型中的信息甄别能力
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地与互联网等外部知识源结合使用。它们能否对信息进行恰当的权衡——即对可靠来源给予更多的信念更新（来源甄别），并在主张使其先验更接近真相时给予更多的更新（真相甄别）？我们将这一问题形式化为“信息甄别”，并提出了Learn2Discern（L2D），这是一个基于三条规范性公理、配备可解释指标的实验框架与基准测试。为确立外部效度，一项预注册、配额匹配的用户研究（n=299）证实，真实的LLM用户认可全部三条公理，并表示违反这些公理会降低他们的信任度和使用意愿。在13个模型、近67万次试验中，研究发现模型在这两个维度上均存在持续性的失败：模型在来源甄别和真相甄别上的表现接近随机水平，其对来源流行度的依赖程度是对来源可靠性的两倍，且无论主张是改善还是恶化其相对真相的立场，模型的更新幅度都大致相同。
tldr: 该论文提出“信息甄别”概念及基于三条规范性公理的Learn2Discern（L2D）基准框架，并通过13个模型近67万次试验与真实用户研究证实，当前大语言模型在来源甄别和真相甄别两个维度上均持续失败、表现接近随机水平。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes "information discernment" and introduces the Learn2Discern (L2D) benchmark grounded in three normative axioms, revealing through ~670K trials across 13 models and a pre-registered user study that current LLMs consistently fail at both source and truth discernment, performing near chance level.
